reports.name: Track M v2
labels: The world's media are PyMC-Marketing's default class: its logistic saturation is the world's tanh curve, and its normalised geometric adstock at the kernel's length is the world's kernel.
Every arm is told the kernel's length.
A geo test is two universes at the market's scale, so its gap holds no noise between regions beyond the noise drawn.

reports.name: PyMC-Marketing's home ground
labels: The world's media are PyMC-Marketing's default class, by the bench's generator: each channel's spend over its largest week through PyMC-Marketing 1.2.0's normalised geometric adstock and its logistic saturation.

Alpha and lam are drawn from PyMC-Marketing's default priors, Beta(1, 3) and Gamma(3, 1), not from Track M v2's ranges; beta is not drawn from its prior but gives each channel the return over the history of the Track M v2 world beneath.
Every arm is told the kernel's length, Track M v2's.
Beneath the media each world is a Track M v2 drawn world: its base, its spend, its measurement layer and its quarter.
A geo test is two universes at the market's scale, so its gap holds no noise between regions beyond the noise drawn.

reports.name: geo
labels: Each geo's effect on a channel is drawn from the hierarchy chc's geo model takes: log-normal about the channel's national median, independent across geos and channels.
A geo's lift is its population times a curve of its spend per head.
Every arm is told the kernel's length.
National media is allotted to the geos by population, so outside its tests every geo spends the same on it a head.
